aboutAuthor: Robin Dreeke is a former FBI counterintelligence agent and head of the FBI's Counterintelligence Behavioral Analysis Program. With collaborator Cameron Stauth, he teaches the Code of Trust as a system for behavior prediction in business and life.

points.heading: Behavior prediction over mind reading
points.body: Dreeke reframes sizing as forecasting future actions from observable behavior in context, using B = P + C and baselining. Illustration: angled chairs that elicit narrative over interrogation, because rapport predicts disclosure better than pressure.

points.heading: Vesting and longevity filter cheap talk
points.body: Alliances are proven by invested time, money, reputation, and relationships, tested via small commitments, and by patterns that persist across success, failure, and boredom, not by recency.

points.heading: Reliability compounds
points.body: Promises kept over promises made, scored as a ratio that inflects below eighty percent, is the most practical sign. Timestamped small deliveries that cost, like 2 a.m. translations, predict big ones.

points.heading: Actions when unwatched are dealbreakers
points.body: How someone treats the powerless or handles random inspections predicts how they will treat you when leverage flips. Divergence between words and unwatched actions, even small theft leakage, is a hard no.

points.heading: Language leaks self-concept
points.body: Pronoun shifts, hedges, and thematic versus chronological stories reveal accountability. A hopefully spike before a restatement shows language forecasting before numbers do, but only in clusters.

points.heading: Stability is recovery speed
points.body: Regulation is measured by time to return to baseline after stress, not by flat affect. Recovery curves and radar polygon aggregation ensure no single sign predicts; the system's area does.

insights: Vesting ladder: ask for a small translation early to see if they invest before it matters.
Rifling the pronoun shift: I to you under stress and mistakes were made distancing as language leak.
Six-sign radar polygon where no single spike predicts but the cluster's area does.
conclusion: Sizing People Up translates FBI elicitation into everyday habit: baseline, cluster six observable signs, and bet on the polygon, not a hunch. Vesting, longevity, reliability, actions, language, and stability together let you build bulletproof alliances and gracefully avoid those who will cost you when it counts.
